Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //wwu.dilg.com.ph OILG OPINION NO. SEP 22 2023 HON. MELVIN K. VARGAS, Jr. Vice Govemor, Province of Cagayan Alimannao, Pefiablanca, Cagayan Dear Hon. Vargas: This pertains to your letter dated June 05, 2023 regarding the request of Govemor Manuel Mamba for the Sangguniang Panlalawigant to adopt a resolution authorizing him to use the unutilized donations during various calamities under the Trust Fund Account of the Provincial Government of Cagayan to settle its remaining obligation of Nine Million Six Hundred Forty Two Thousand Three Hundred Thirty Eight Pesos and Thirty Seven Centavos (P9,642,338.37) to Prime Gigabuild Construction Corporation for the project Construction of Warehouse Building (Food and Non-food Storage) located at Sub-Capitol, Bangag, Lallo, Cagayan, with a total contract price of Thirteen Million Nine Hundred Seventy Five Thousand Four Hundred Fifty One Pesos and Thirty Seven Centavos (P13,975,451.37). The issues raised are quoted in toto as follows: 1. Is the approval of the resolution of the matter in accordance with the pertinent laws, rules and regulations considering that these donations were already reverted to the National Treasury? 2. Are there any violations forthe non-utilization ofthe said donations to the Provincial Govemment? We take notice of how the first query was phrased, that the donations were already reverted to the National Treasury. However, as stated in the Governors request for fund utilization through a letter dated January 26, 2023, it was attested that the Provincial Accountant certified available balances of unutilized donations to the province dating back to 2008, viz: CALAMITY Typhoon Goring, Narsing, Ilian Typhoon Typhoon Province Ondoy and Juan (Albay PARTICULARS Forwarded balance Janu 01, 2008 Received on December 17, 2009, RCD 12-188 from Provincial Govemor of Quirino Received on November 15, 2010 RCD 11-159 as Collection of PGA Financial Assistance BALANCE P 81,366.73 P 100,000.00 P 250,000 "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan"

Typhoon Pedring Quiel Typhoon Lawin Typhoon Ompong and Received on October 12, Oplan Tulong Cagayan TOTAL 2011 RCD 10-173 from Landbank of the Phili ines Collection from October 28, 2016-various donors Collection from October 01, 2018-various donors Collection from November 12, 2019 — various donors from Typhoon Quiel, T hoon Ramon P 200,000.00 P 276,211.58 P 4,472,988.03 P 10,608,226.35 What was mentioned as reverted back to the National Treasury was the unexpended balance out of the original fund of the construction project under the National Disaster Risk Reduction Management Fund (NDRRMF) FY 2020 General Appropriations Act (GAA), Republic Act 11465, as the same fund expired before the completion of said project. Hence, the recent request to utilize the available balances of unutilized donations from various calamities for the payment of the warehouse construction project. Considering that the issues propounded were interrelated, we shall address the issues in one discussion, succinctly. In the context of "Trust Fund", utilization thereof is strictly limited to the specific purpose for which it was created or for which it came into possession of the local government unit. Section 309 (b) of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known the "Local Government Code of 1991 " is controlling: "Section 309. Special Funds. — There shall be maintained in every provincial, city, or. Municipal treasury the following special funds: (b) Trust funds which shall consist of private and public monies which have officially come into the possession of the local government or a local government official a trustee, agent or administrator, or which have been received as a guaranty for the fulfillment of some obligation. A trust fund shall only be used for the specific purpose for which it was created or for which it came into the possession of the local government unit." (Emphasis Supplied) Corollary thereto, Section 45( 2), Chapter 8, Title I (B), Book V, of Executive Order 292, provides: SECTION 45. Disbursement of Government Funds.—(l) Revenue funds shall not be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority; (2) Trust funds shall not be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in fulfillment of the purpose for which the trust was created or funds received, and upon authorization of the legislative body, or head of any other agency of the government having control thereof, and

subject to pertinent budget laws, rules and regulations; (Emphasis Supplied) In addition, the Government Auditing Code of the Philippines or PD 1445 mandates, among others, that Trust Funds shall be available and may be spent only for the specific purpose for which the trust was created or the funds received. The Trust Funds under consideration herein are donations from other LGUs, private individuals and entities to address the need of the local community as a form of disaster risk assistance. The recipient LGU, therefore, is only allowed to utilize said fund strictly for the purpose of addressing the aftermath of the calamities for which that funds were donated. Thus, the funds are intended as an aid generally for disaster risk reduction activities and projects. Specifically for the total amount of P 10,608,226.35 which constitutes the unexpended balances from donations during various calamities, the allowed expenditures would be programs and projects for purposes aligned to supporting the disaster risk reduction and management plan of the province. That allowed expenditures include the utilization of the accumulated unexpended balances for the settlement of remaining obligation on the project Construction of Warehouse Building (Food and Non-food Storage) if the same is for the purpose of storing relief goods and disaster response equipment as a form of disaster preparedness and risk reduction efforts of the provincial government. Why is this opinion on this tenor and how does it defer to other opinions discussing the need for reversion of unexpended balances of trust funds to the National Treasury? Let us expound further to address possible confusion on the matter. For this purpose we make reference to Section 28, Chapter 4, Executive Order No. 292: SECTION 28. Reversion of Unexpended Balances of Appropriations, Continuing Appropriations.—Unexpended balances of appropriations authorized in the General Appropriation Act shall revert to the unappropriated surplus of the General Fund at the end of the fiscal year and shall not thereafter be available for expenditure except by subsequent legislative enactment: Provided, that appropriations for capital outlays shall remain valid until fully spent or reverted: Provided, further, that continuing appropriations for current operating expenditures may be specifically recommended and approved as such in support of projects whose effective implementation calls for multi-year expenditure commitments: Provided, finally, that the President may authorize the use of savings realized by an agency during a given year to meet non- recurring expenditures in a subsequent year. The reversion of unexpended balances of appropriations under Section 28, Chapter 4, Executive Order No. 292, applies to those covered by appropriations authorized under the General Appropriations Act (GAA). That includes special trust funds if funded by the GAA, an example of which is the Local Disaster Risk Reduction & Management Fund (LDRRMF). LGUs are obligated to revert the unexpended balance from that special trust account to the National Treasury after the timeframe set by the specific GAA (fund source) which authorized the utilization thereof. On the other hand, the peculiarity of the trust fund under consideration in this instant case is that it did not come from the general fund of the government. It came from donations of public corporations, private individuals and entities. Hence, the legal compliance that governs is the above-cited Section 45( 2), Chapter 8, Title I (B), Book V, of Executive Order

292, (1) the need for a legislative authorization before a trust fund may be paid out of the public treasury or depository and (2) that the utilization is in accord to the purpose for which the it was created. This opinion is herein issued without prejudice to contrary opinion which may be issued by competent government agencies and/or a decision of the proper courts. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, Byt Autho •ty of the Secretary: VICT .
